newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt arrests Algerian with money for militants.
newsitem.headline: Egypt arrests Algerian with money for militants.

text.p: Egyptian police have arrested an Algerian woman they say came to Egypt to give Moslem militants money and orders from an exiled leader to carry out attacks, the Interior Ministry said on Thursday.

Police found 42,000 pounds ($12,000), a firearm and literature of the violent militant Jihad (Holy War) Group when they arrested Djamila Ma'ali al-Falaki on Wednesday, the ministry said in a statement.
Jihad, which assassinated president Anwar Sadat in 1981, is one of several groups fighting to overthrow the Egyptian government and set up a strict Islamic state.
It said leading Jihad member Yasser Tawfiq Ali el-Serri had recruited Falaki and sent her to Egypt to give militants money to revive Jihad activity in Egypt and prepare for attacts in the country.

Serri is on the run from a number of prison terms and a death sentence for trying to kill former Egyptian prime minister Atef Sedki. He lives in London where he runs the International Islamic Observatory which projects the Islamist point of view on events in the Middle East.
The Interior Ministry said Falaki had passed on Serri's instructions to three lawyers who it says are members of Jihad. It did not name them.
More than 1,000 people have died in political violence in Egypt since militants launched their anti-government campaign in 1992.
